newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas pares losses, still ends mostly down.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas pares losses, still ends mostly down.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures pared early losses Thursday but still ended mostly lower in moderate trade, as forecasts for colder weather this week and next were offset by Wednesday's bearish AGA report.
February closed down by 3.2 cents at $3.481 per million British thermal units after skidding early to $3.25. March settled nine cents lower at $3.086. Some 1998s ended up.

"The weather looks bullish for the next week or two, but it's going to be tough to test the old highs given the storage situation," said one Texas trader, adding the next mild weather forecast could send the market sharply lower.

AGA data showed U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 15 bcf, well-below expectations in the 70-85 bcf range. Stocks are now 69 bcf above year-ago levels, the first time in more than a year that overall inventories are in surplus to year-ago. And eastern storage stands 211 bcf, or almost 20 percent, above last year.

While Arctic weather may limit aggressive selling near-term, traders said more comfortable inventory levels should temper the bulls. And with cash to futures spreads still in steep backwardation, most agreed operators at some point soon will look to dump storage and cash in.

Technically, traders still pegged February support in the remaining gap between $3.11 and $3.25, with better buying likely in the $2.60s. Resistance was seen at $3.57 and then in the $3.80-3.84 area and at $3.96. The contract high is $4.02.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped Thursday by 15-20 cents to the $3.60 area. Midcontinent pipes were down about a nickel to the low-$3.80s. New York city gate gas was talked on either side of $4.00, off about 30 cents on the day.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell 3.2 cents to $2.472.
NYMEX said an estimated 40,866 Hub contracts traded, down slightly from Wednesday's revised tally of 41,753.

NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Thursday. On the KCBT, February closed down one cent at $3.32, while deferred months finished one to seven cents lower. The East/West spread narrowed by 2.2 cents to 16.1 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 360 contracts traded, up slightly from Wednesday's total of 337.
